q: 1. The shear strength of soil
options: increases with an increase in the normal stress
is proportional to the cohesion of the soil
is generally known as the strength of the soil
explain: By Coulomb's equation s = c + σ tanφ, shear strength increases with normal stress and cohesion, and is generally regarded as the overall 'strength' of soil — all statements are correct.

q: 2. On wetting, cohesive solid,
explain: Increased moisture reduces inter-particle attraction and increases pore pressure in cohesive soils, thereby decreasing their shear strength.

q: 3. Which of the following soils has largest permeability?
explain: Gravel has the largest particle size and pore spaces of these soils, giving it the highest permeability.

q: 4. As the value of drainage path increases the time required for consolidation will .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked indeterminate; by consolidation theory (Tv = Cv t/d^2), a longer drainage path normally increases the time required.

q: 5. The degree of consolidation is proportional directly
options: to time and inversely to drainage path
to drainage path and inversely to time
to time and inversely to the square of drainage path
to square of drainage path and inversely to time
explain: The time factor Tv = Cv·t/d² shows degree of consolidation increases with time t and decreases with the square of the drainage path length d.

q: 6. Hygroscopic water can be removed by
explain: Hygroscopic water is held to particle surfaces by molecular attraction, far stronger than gravity, so it can only be removed by heating (oven drying), not by gravity or free flow.

q: 7. The property of a soil which permits water to percolate through it, is called
explain: Permeability is defined as the property of a porous medium (soil) that allows water to flow (percolate) through its voids.

q: 8. The value of mobilized cohesion will be .............
explain: For local/punching shear conditions, mobilized shear parameters are reduced; cohesion is typically taken as 2/3 of the actual cohesion C (Terzaghi's approach).

q: 9. The critical exit gradient of the seepage of water in a soil is
explain: The critical hydraulic gradient (at which quicksand condition initiates) equals (G-1)/(1+e), derived by equating seepage force to submerged weight.

q: 10. The compression resulting from long term static load and resulting expulsion of water is known as
explain: Time-dependent volume reduction of saturated soil under sustained load, due to gradual expulsion of pore water, defines consolidation.

q: 11. Absorbed water in soil is
options: the water chemically combined in crystal structure of the soil material
having free movement through the soil by gravity
water absorbed from atmosphere by forces of attraction
explain: Absorbed (structural/adsorbed) water refers to water molecules chemically bound within the crystal lattice of clay minerals, distinct from free or hygroscopic water.

q: 12. A coarse grained soil has a void ratio of 0.7 and specific gravity of 2.7. The critical gradient at which the quick sand condition occurs is .............
13. In the case of retaining walls, surcharge is
options: additional load carrying capacity of wall
extra load on the horizontal backfill
explain: Surcharge refers to any additional load (e.g., traffic, stacked material) placed on the horizontal backfill surface behind a retaining wall, which increases lateral pressure.

q: 14. A grillage foundation is used under
explain: Grillage foundations use layers of steel beams to spread heavy column loads over a large area economically, typically under a single heavily loaded isolated column.

q: 15. If h is the head of water stored, Nf is the number of flow lines and Nd is the number of equipotential drops in a flow net, then the seepage flow rate is given by
explain: The standard flow-net discharge formula is q = k·h·(Nf/Nd), where Nf/Nd is the shape factor of the flow net.

q: 16. The strength theory applicable to a C-φ soil is
explain: A c-φ (cohesive-frictional) soil's shear strength is described by the Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion, s = c + σ·tanφ.

q: 17. Even after the complete dissipation of excess pore pressure, a little more consolidation is possible. This is called as .............
explain: Secondary consolidation is the slow, creep-like compression that continues after primary consolidation (pore pressure dissipation) is complete.

q: 18. The angle of internal friction depends upon
explain: Friction angle is influenced by particle shape/roughness, degree of interlocking (density/angularity), and the normal stress level — all these factors jointly affect φ.

q: 19. The type of settlement which causes more trouble for the stability of structure is .............
explain: Differential (uneven) settlement causes structural distortion and cracking, making it far more damaging than uniform settlement.

q: 20. For calculating stress distribution in soils, Boussinesq assumed point load to be
explain: Boussinesq's classical elastic theory for stress distribution assumes a concentrated point load applied at the ground surface (ground level) of a semi-infinite, homogeneous, isotropic elastic medium.

q: 21. Maximum failures of earth dams are due to
options: Erosion of soil due to flowing water
Leakage through cavities or holes formed by animals
explain: Historically, the most common cause of earth dam failure is erosion/piping of soil caused by uncontrolled seepage/overtopping flowing water eroding the embankment.

q: 22. In a flow net
options: Flow lines and equipotential lines meet at right angles to one another
Quantity of water flowing through each flow channel is different
Larger the dimensions of the field, smaller will be the hydraulic gradient
Different potential drop occurs between two successive equipotential lines
explain: A defining property of a properly constructed flow net is that flow lines and equipotential lines always intersect orthogonally (at right angles), forming curvilinear squares.

q: 23. Consolidation theory was due to
explain: Karl Terzaghi formulated the classical one-dimensional theory of consolidation, a cornerstone of modern soil mechanics.

q: 24. The hydrostatic pressure on the phreatic line within a dam section is .............
explain: The phreatic line is the top flow line where pore pressure equals atmospheric (zero gauge) pressure by definition.

q: 25. Consolidation theory was enunciated by .............
explain: Terzaghi developed the classical one-dimensional theory of consolidation, the foundation of modern soil mechanics.

q: 26. Choose the correct statement
options: confined aquifer is at upper level and unconfined aquiifer is at lower level under the ground
confined is temporary and unconfined is permanent under the ground
confined is unsaturated and unconfined is saturated under the ground
confined aquifer is at lower level and unconfined aquifer is at upper level under the ground
explain: Typically, an unconfined (water table) aquifer lies near the ground surface, while a confined (artesian) aquifer, trapped between impermeable layers, lies at a deeper level.

q: 27. A clay deposit suffers a total settlement of 10 cm with one way drainage, then with two way drainage, it suffers a total settlement of .............
explain: Total (final) consolidation settlement depends only on the applied stress and soil compressibility, not on the drainage path — so it remains 10 cm; drainage path only affects the rate of settlement.

q: 28. Magnitude of capillary rise is more in .............
explain: Clay has the smallest pore sizes, producing the highest capillary rise due to greater surface tension effects in narrower channels.

q: 29. Piping in soils is due to .............
options: erosion of subsoil by high velocity of seepage flow
leakage of water through pipes laid in dams
passage of water through well-connected pores in soil
explain: Per the reference key this is marked as leakage through pipes in dams; the classical geotechnical definition of piping is progressive erosion caused by high-velocity seepage flow.

q: 30. Units of co-efficient of permeability .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked s^2/cm; the standard, correct unit for coefficient of permeability is actually cm/s (a velocity unit).

q: 31. The space factor of a flow net is defined as .............
explain: The space (shape) factor of a flow net is defined as the ratio of number of flow channels to number of equipotential drops, Nf/Nd.

q: 32. The u/s face of an earth dam is .............
explain: The upstream (submerged) face of an earth dam, being in contact with reservoir water at constant head, acts as an equipotential line.

q: 33. The quantity of seepage in a soil is .............
options: directly proportional to the coefficient of permeability
inversely proportional to the coefficient of permeability
directly proportional to the uniformity coefficient of the soil
explain: By Darcy's law, seepage discharge is directly proportional to permeability (q = kiA).

q: 34. Flow net is used for the determination of .............
explain: A flow net simultaneously allows determination of exit gradient, total seepage quantity, and pore/hydrostatic pressures at any point.

q: 35. If consolidation experiments are conducted on two soil samples of the same soil but having different thickness (thick and thin) then the deformations will be higher in .............
explain: Total settlement is proportional to layer thickness under the same effective stress increment, so the thicker sample undergoes greater overall deformation.
